result.label: Indicator - Volunteering
note:
[b]Volunteering[/b]

[b]How do we measure this?[/b]
Percentage of adults volunteering.

[b]Source[/b]
Experience of volunteering by adults in Northern Ireland, Department for Communities 
[url=https://www.communities-ni.gov.uk/topics/voluntary-and-community-statistics]Voluntary and community statistics | Department for Communities[/url]

[b]Impact of Covid-19[/b]
None, since baseline is 2023/24.

[b]Further Information[/b]
1. New questions on volunteering were introduced in 2023/24 to measure participation of adults in both formal and informal volunteering. The questions are now more similar to those used in the rest of the UK. As a result of the change in questions it is not possible to compare figures for 2023/24 and 2024/25 with those published for previous years.

[b]Deprivation[/b]
2. Figures above are based on the 2017 NIMDM. More information on the NI Multiple Deprivation Measures can be found here:
[url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation[/url]

[b]Urban Rural[/b]
3. All figures are defined according to the 2015 urban rural classification. More information on Urban Rural classifications can be found here:
[url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/support/geography/urban-rural-classification]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/support/geography/urban-rural-classification[/url]

[b]Religion[/b]
4. 'Other/no religion' includes those who stated a religion other than Catholic and Protestant, and those who stated no religion.

[b]Disability[/b]
5. For this indicator, ‘disability’ is measured using ‘limiting long-standing illness’. Respondents are defined as having a limiting long standing illness if they have any physical or mental health conditions or illnesses lasting or expected to last for 12 months or more, and the condition(s) or illness(es) reduce their ability to carry out day to day activities.

[b]Dependants[/b]
6. For this indicator, 'has dependants' includes individuals who have responsibility for the care of: a child(ren); a person with a disability; and/or a dependant elderly person.

[b]Volunteering type[/b]
7. Volunteering can be formal or informal. Formal volunteering involves giving time through groups, clubs or organisations, while informal volunteering includes unpaid help given directly to individuals or to improve the local environment, outside of any organised group. Both forms of volunteering are unpaid and done by choice.
